subject: AI & Agents
title: How AI Reads Text
description: A quick win: understand How AI Reads Text.

hook.text: You read words. AI reads numbers. Every word gets converted into a long list of digits.

buildup.text: Tokenizers chop sentences into pieces — words, subwords, or even single characters.

discovery.text: Each token maps to a vector — a point in high-dimensional space where meaning lives.

twist.text: 'King' minus 'man' plus 'woman' equals 'queen' — in vector math, meaning is arithmetic.

climax.text: This trick lets AI grasp synonyms, analogies, and context without ever reading a dictionary.

punchline.text: To an AI, every word is a coordinate on a map.

quiz.question: How does AI represent words internally?
options: As numerical vectors in high-dimensional space

details.summary: AI reads text by breaking it into tokens — word pieces or characters — and converting them into numerical vectors. These vectors capture meaning relationships and are processed through layers of neural network computation.
details.whyItMatters: Knowing how AI processes text explains its strengths and weaknesses. It excels at pattern matching and generation but processes meaning statistically, without true comprehension.
takeaways: Text is split into tokens and converted to numerical vectors
Vectors capture statistical relationships between words
The process enables powerful pattern matching without comprehension

faq.question: What exactly is a token in AI?
faq.answer: A token is a chunk of text the model processes as one unit. It can be a whole word, part of a word, or a single character. The word 'understanding' might be split into 'under' and 'standing' as two tokens.

faq.question: Why does AI sometimes struggle with simple text tasks?
faq.answer: Tokenization can split words in ways that lose meaning. Counting letters, reversing text, and understanding certain wordplay are hard because the model sees token chunks, not individual characters.
